user.title: Connect to Windmill
user.description: Enter the Windmill instance URL and a token with at least `users:read` access. The token is only ever sent in an authorization header.

data_description.base_url: For example {cloud_url} or the URL of your self-hosted instance. Plain HTTP works too, but sends the token unencrypted.
data_description.token: A least-privilege Windmill user token. Add `workspaces:read` if you want to pick the workspace from a list.

workspace.title: Select a workspace
workspace.description: Choose the workspace this entry should monitor. If your token cannot list workspaces, type the workspace ID manually.

data_description.workspace: The workspace ID, not its display name.

capabilities.title: Detected capabilities

features.title: Select features
features.description: Enable only what you need. Administrative and high-cardinality monitoring stays disabled unless you turn it on, and a feature whose capability is unavailable will simply create no entities.

data_description.detailed_health: Administrative: needs a token that Windmill accepts on the detailed health endpoint.
data_description.worker_groups: Administrative: exposes alive workers and version drift per worker group.
data_description.worker_details: High cardinality: adds one entity per worker instance and is meant for self-hosted operators.
data_description.update_entity: Self-hosted only. Managed Windmill Cloud deployments are updated by Windmill.
data_description.runnable_buttons: Optional: adds one button per selected runnable that needs no arguments. The action stays available either way.
data_description.run_scope: Narrows the run sensors and the run event entity to selected scripts and flows or to jobs this integration started. A scope change never replays older completions.

reauth_confirm.title: Update the Windmill token
reauth_confirm.description: Enter a new token for workspace {workspace} on {base_url}. The instance and workspace of this entry stay unchanged.

reconfigure.title: Reconfigure the Windmill connection
reconfigure.description: Change the instance URL or workspace of this entry. Leave the token empty to keep the current one.

data_description.token: Optional. The stored token is kept when this field stays empty.

error.insufficient_permission: The token cannot access this workspace.
error.invalid_url: Enter a valid HTTP or HTTPS URL without credentials, query or fragment.
error.invalid_workspace: The workspace is invalid or unavailable.

abort.already_configured: This Windmill instance and workspace are already configured.

features.title: Windmill features
features.description: Enable only the features you need. Changes reload the integration.

runnables.title: Select scripts and flows
runnables.description: Only the runnables you select here can ever be exposed by Home Assistant. Discovery is bounded, so very large workspaces may not list every runnable.

data.pin_selected: Pin newly selected runnables to their current version

data_description.pin_selected: Pinned scripts keep their current hash and pinned flows their current version. Runnables you already selected keep their existing mode.

run.description: Starts a selected Windmill script or flow asynchronously and returns its job identifier.

config_entry_id.name: Windmill workspace
config_entry_id.description: The configured Windmill instance and workspace to run in.

kind.name: Kind
kind.description: Whether the runnable is a script or a flow.

path.description: Path of a runnable you selected in the integration options.

arguments.name: Arguments
arguments.description: JSON-compatible arguments validated against the runnable's input schema.

cancel.name: Cancel a job
cancel.description: Cancels a job that Home Assistant started and still tracks.

config_entry_id.name: Windmill workspace

job_id.description: Identifier returned by the run action.

unknown_config_entry.message: The selected Windmill entry does not exist.

entry_not_loaded.message: The selected Windmill entry is not loaded.

runnable_not_selected.message: {path} is not selected in the Windmill integration options.

runnable_unsupported.message: {path} has arguments this integration cannot validate.

arguments_too_large.message: The arguments exceed the supported size.

invalid_argument_value.message: Argument {name} is not an allowed value.

pin_unavailable.message: {path} is pinned, but Windmill does not expose a version to pin to. Select it again without pinning.

job_not_tracked.message: Home Assistant did not start job {job_id}, or it is no longer tracked.

job_not_cancellable.message: Job {job_id} is already finished or cannot be cancelled.

insecure_transport.title: Windmill is reached over unencrypted HTTP
insecure_transport.description: This integration talks to `{host}` over plain HTTP, so the Windmill token and every job payload travel unencrypted and can be read or altered by anyone on the network path. This is accepted for a self-hosted instance without a certificate. To remove this message, put a TLS-terminating reverse proxy in front of Windmill and reconfigure the integration to the `https://` URL.

missing_permission.title: Windmill permission missing for an enabled feature
missing_permission.description: The Windmill token used by this integration is not allowed to read `{capability}`, which the enabled `{feature}` feature needs. Grant the permission to the token in Windmill, or turn the feature off in the integration options. This message disappears on its own once the permission works again.

unsupported_capability.title: Windmill does not support an enabled feature
unsupported_capability.description: This Windmill instance does not offer the `{capability}` endpoint that the enabled `{feature}` feature needs, usually because the server is older than the feature. Upgrade Windmill, or turn the feature off in the integration options.

worker_version_drift.title: Windmill worker group runs several versions
worker_version_drift.description: The `{group}` worker group has been running {versions} different Windmill versions for more than 30 minutes. During a rolling upgrade this is expected and no message is shown; lasting drift usually means a worker failed to upgrade. Check the workers of that group in Windmill.
